ground_truth.description: The set_task_status verification rule says to increment the success counter (e.g. tasks_reopened) whenever newStatus matches the requested status. A no-op call (task already in the requested status) has newStatus == requested, so it is over-counted as a successful operation. The later-corrected version explicitly added a `"no_op": true` branch that skips the increment, confirming this omission over-reports counters and defeats the task's goal of verifying real operation success.

The guidance counts status="combined" toward tasks_created, but a combined ticket was merged into an existing task (no new task created, per lines 41-42), so incrementing tasks_created inflates the creation count.

The set_task_status response contract is described only as a single per-task record (tasks[n] with camelCase taskId/oldStatus/newStatus) and omits the comma-separated-list wrapper ({"success": bool, "results": [...]}) and per-id result.error cases. An agent applying the top-level newStatus rule to a batched call, or encountering a per-id error, will mis-count or spuriously flag/escalate a discrepancy — consistent with the review-passed-but-escalation-created symptom. Field naming is also inconsistent (taskId camelCase vs task_id snake_case used elsewhere).

provenance.runs_db_query: SELECT task_id, project_id, outcome, review_cycles, verify_attempts FROM task_results WHERE review_cycles >= 1, cross-referenced with events (escalation_created, merge_finalized) -- see mining.mine_fn_candidates.
